answer: A numbered falcon carries a cipher tag on its leg band; its return to a prism-marked perch is the proof. The holder visits once, the falconer releases it, and it lands on the perch as the keeper notes the tag with the date. Two verifiers watch a second release in 24 hours and match tag and number; a bird never released there or a duplicate number locks and burns the deposit. One release is cheap; 100 fakes need 100 trained falcons and 100 trips.
